newsitem.title: GREECE: Greenpeace slams Greek power policy as hazardous.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace slams Greek power policy as hazardous.

text.p: Greenpeace activists swung from the seven-storey building of Greece's state power company DEH on Tuesday to hang a huge poster alleging that the firm is the country's worst air polluter.
Dozens of bystanders watched in awe as activists hooked up the giant banner, which read "Clean Solutions Now", on the glass and concrete building in central Athens.
Other members of the international environmental group, holding placards reading "Go Solar", blocked the entrance to the DEH officies.
"So far, unfortunately Greece has taken no steps to promote solar energy," Holger Ronitz, a press officer for Greenpeace international, told Reuters.
Greenpeace accuses DEH of ignoring renewable energy sources abundant in Greece, such as sun and wind, and depending almost exclusively on fossil fuel.
"DEH is responsible for 50 percent of Greece's total carbon dioxide emissions and can claim the title of number one polluter in Greece," said Greenpeace solar campaigner Stelios Psomas.
